**Newsroom brief: IBM's software-led rebound faces a broader demand test**

IBM's Q3 recovery leans on software.

**Context:** The strongest countercase is that software revenue rose in every same-quarter comparison and its segment profit margin improved.

Read the article: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/pending-publication-b39e88587862e50c

Operating cash flow increased by $2,638 million. The larger IBM Financing-receivables adjustment removes $1,900 million of that increase, and higher net capital spending removes $133 million. IBM-defined free cash flow rose by a reported $606 million, from $7,181 million to $7,787 million. Arithmetic on the rounded components yields $605 million, a $1 million difference from the reported gain. IBM-defined free cash flow is non-GAAP. These are consolidated IBM figures, not Software cash conversion or a full cash-balance bridge. Financing amounts are quantities removed; net capital expenditures retain their reported negative signs. Reported levels (USD million, 2025 / 2026): GAAP operating cash flow 9,153 / 11,791; Financing-receivables change removed 905 / 2,805; net capital expenditures -1,067 / -1,200; IBM-defined free cash flow 7,181 / 7,787. Source: IBM Q3 2026 earnings release, October 21, 2026; nine-month cash-flow reconciliation. Sources: [IBM · 21 Oct 2026](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-10-21-IBM-RELEASES-THIRD-QUARTER-RESULTS).
